title: Chest Wound (Penetrating or Open)
summary: A wound to the chest can damage the lungs. Control bleeding, leave an open chest wound uncovered or use a non-sealing dressing, and watch breathing closely.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for any penetrating chest wound
when: Any stab, gunshot or impalement wound to the chest, back or upper abdomen
Difficulty breathing, coughing blood or blue lips

steps.title: Make it safe and call {EMERGENCY}
steps.text: Weapons or the cause of the injury may still be present. Wear gloves.

steps.title: Help them into the easiest position to breathe
steps.text: Usually half-sitting, leaning towards the injured side.

steps.title: Leave an open chest wound open
steps.text: Do not seal it. Leave it exposed, or if a dressing is needed, use a non-occlusive (non-sealing) dressing.
steps.caution: Do not tape a sealed dressing or plastic over an open chest wound – trapped air can make breathing much worse.

steps.title: Control bleeding
steps.text: Apply direct pressure with a dressing over bleeding points.

steps.title: Do not remove impaled objects
steps.text: Pad around anything stuck in the wound to stop it moving.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Watch breathing and response closely and be ready to start CPR.

doNot: Do not apply an airtight (occlusive) dressing to an open chest wound
Do not remove an impaled object
Do not give food or drink

sources.title: International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)
sources.section: First Aid – Dressings for open chest wounds

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
